title: Noise Attenuation Blanket Set for the Auran 7000 Fan Cowl Interior
abstract: Proposal to line the interior of the fan cowl doors with a shaped attenuation blanket, addressing the tonal content that three airports have flagged in their noise-related landing charge assessments.

sections.reason: Three European airports moved in 2025 to a charging scheme that assesses tonal content separately from the overall certificated noise level, and the Evo variant scores worse on tone than its overall level would suggest. Measurement traced the dominant tone to a cavity resonance between the fan case and the cowl door inner skin, which is excited at a narrow band of fan speeds used in the approach configuration. The certificated noise level is unaffected and there is no airworthiness item here; the driver is the landing charge, which one operator puts at 220 kEUR per aircraft per year on its European network.
sections.description: A shaped attenuation blanket is bonded to the inner face of each fan cowl door, tuned to the cavity depth rather than applied as a uniform layer. The right-hand cowl door nozzle assembly D7110118543283 is re-worked where the blanket edge lands on it, and the obsolete inboard heat shield ROS257338-24 is deleted because the blanket takes over its function. Shear head bolts AES484712-68 retain the blanket edge strips and the blanket is additionally secured with cable ties EN504744-1D at the cowl stiffeners. The forward cowl latch shroud kit AR674643-02 is re-cut where the thicker lining reduces the clearance to the latch handle. The upper duct position 43EN and the lower duct position 5EN9 both pass behind the blanket and require re-clipping, and the upper latch clamp position 3741PP9 is re-set to the new closed dimension. Work is with the fan cowl doors open, zones 452, 454 and 462. Detail is on drawing D71101245330.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 16 kg per engine. No electrical load change. The blanket is interchangeable at cowl door level but the door cannot be closed with a mixed blanket and heat shield installation because the clearance to the latch handle would be lost. Predicted tonal reduction is 2.4 EPNdB in the approach band with no measurable change in the certificated levels, which means the noise certificate is not re-issued and the benefit is purely commercial. Fan cowl opening and closing tasks require a revised clearance note, and the cowl door removal task gains a blanket handling caution.
sections.embodiment_note: Proposal only. If launched, embodiment would be at any line maintenance opportunity where the cowl doors can be opened, estimated at nine hours per engine. Bonding cure time is the limiting item and would normally be done off the aircraft on a spare cowl door.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must confirm the blanket flammability qualification against the current cowl fire zone classification, whether the deleted heat shield has any residual function in the fire case, and whether the tonal benefit measured on the test engine transfers to the in-service fan speed line.

type_data.balance_impact: Symmetric about the centre line; no reportable effect
type_data.production_impact: No cut-in proposed at proposal stage
